annotation.title_clean: Data regulation in the age of AI and other data‑intensive technologies
annotation.title_en: Data regulation in the age of AI and other data‑intensive technologies
annotation.authors_or_issuer: UK Government (Department for Science, Innovation and Technology), GOV.UK
annotation.summary_en: UK Government call for evidence (15 July–9 September 2026) on how personal and non-personal data regulation, especially UK GDPR, interacts with AI and data-intensive technologies. It covers five themes: data access, quality and fairness, cross-organisational governance, transparency and rights, and framework effectiveness. Embodied AI is mentioned only in passing.
key_provisions_or_claims: Open call for evidence from 15 July to 9 September 2026 on data regulation and AI
Five themes: access and use, quality and fairness, governance across organisations, transparency and rights, framework effectiveness
Asks whether guidance, targeted changes or fundamental reform of data protection is needed
Covers automated decision-making, controller/processor roles and agentic AI
Mentions transparency for operating embodied AI systems in real-world environments
